title: Set up atomic configurations and sampling grids
action: Construct relaxed adatom-free geometries for Si(111) surface, [\overline{211}] step, and [\overline{\Pi2}] step using the Si(111) lattice and the Stillinger-Weber potential. Define the triangular sampling grid (surface, one sixth of the surface unit cell, spacing a₂/9) and the rectangular grids (steps, spacings a₁/16 along x and a/30 along y) covering the symmetrically distinct regions, matching the paper’s description. Fix bottom bilayers and in‑plane boundaries.
description: Prepare the simulation cells and generate the (x,y) grid points where the adatom will be held fixed.

title: Map adatom potential energy V(x,y)
action: For the surface, [\overline{211}] step, and [\overline{\Pi2}] step configurations: place an adatom at each grid point, keep its (x,y) coordinates fixed, relax the system using MD with dissipation followed by steepest‑descent minimization, and compute the adatom potential V = E(adat‑free) − E(adat‑fixed). Store all grid point coordinates and V values.
description: Run the Stillinger‑Weber potential calculations on the grids. The evidence file must contain the grid coordinates and corresponding V values for each region.
output_schema: A JSON object with keys "surface", "step_211", "step_112"; each key maps to an object with arrays "x", "y", "V" of the same length, holding the grid points and their potential energies in eV.

title: Locate minima, saddle points, and compute barriers
action: Using the potential energy data from step02, exploit the symmetries of the (111) plane to locate the global minimum (H₃ site) and the relevant saddle point for H₃↔H₃ surface diffusion. For step configurations, locate the barrier‑determining saddle points far from the step edge and at the step edge. Compute the surface diffusion barrier as V(saddle) − V(global minimum) and the Schwoebel barriers as the difference between the barrier‑determining saddle energy on the step configuration and the surface barrier‑determining saddle energy s₁. Write the three barriers to a JSON file.
description: Extract the surface diffusion barrier and the two Schwoebel barriers from the V(x,y) maps. The verifier will recompute the barriers from the potential_surface_data.json evidence and compare to hidden paper‑reported values.
